tip: The -았/었음 (-eosseum) ending turns a past clause into a noun of fact: 사람이었음 (saramieosseum) = the fact that they were people. Written Korean states realizations this compactly.
것인지도 모른다 (geosinjido moreunda) = 'it may well be that...' – 지도 모르다 (jido moreuda), literally 'don't even know if', is Korean's soft hedge for musings.
-는다고 해서 ... 아니다 = just because...not: 유지된다고 해서 (yujidoendago haeseo = just because it lasts).
-(으)ㄴ데도 (-ndedo) = 'even though it's so': 법인데도 (beobindedo) = even though that's how it tends to be. One ending does the work of a whole 'and yet' clause.
Korean often names the topic first, then the subject: 후배는 (hubaeneun = as for the junior) sets the frame, 자신감이 (jasingami = confidence) is what is lacking.
것이다 affirms a truth: 진실인 것이다 (jinsirin geosida = it is indeed true).
-곤 했다 marks a repeated past habit: 바라보곤 했다 (barabogon haetda = would gaze).
-더라 reports what you saw firsthand: 들어서 있더라 (deureoseo itdeora = they'd sprung up, I noticed).
-던 것이다 marks a literary reveal: 아내였던 것이다 (anaeyeotdeon geosida) = 'she was, it turns out, his wife'. The 것이다 (geosida) ending stamps the sentence as the story's key fact.
-(으)ㄴ 것이었다 closes a scene with revelation: 도착한 것이었다 (dochakan geosieotda = it had finally arrived).
시작하다 (sijakada = to begin) needs the -기 (-gi) noun form before it – you begin 'the stacking', not 'to stack': 쌓기 시작했다 (ssaki sijakaetda) = began stacking.
-고 있었던 것이다 = past continuous + emphasis: 바치고 있었던 것이다 (bachigo isseotdeon geosida = had been devoting).
-던 recalls a habitual past scene: 앉던 자리 (antteon jari = the seat he always sat in).
-던 모양이다 = 'seems it was (in the past)': 했던 모양이다 (haetdeon moyangida = seems he was).
-던 날 = 'the day when': 태어나던 날 (taeeonadeon nal = the day I was born).
-(으)ㄹ 뿐이었다 = 'did nothing but': 바라볼 뿐이었다 (barabol ppunieotda = only gazed).
-(으)ㄴ 것이 lets a whole past clause be the sentence's subject: 꺼내지 못한 것이 (kkeonaeji motan geosi) = 'his failing to take it out' – that entire event does the changing.
-았을 것이다 = a 'would have' about what did not happen: 포기했을 것이다 (pogihaesseul geosida = we would have given up).
-(으)ㄴ 것이다 stresses the cause: 키운 것이다 (kiun geosida = that is what raised us).
-(으)ㄴ 것이다 marks narrative closure: 끝난 것이다 (kkeunnan geosida = the long journey had ended).
-(으)ㄴ 채 = 'in the state of, without': 속하지 못한 채 (sokaji motan chae = without belonging).
-(으)므로 is a formal 'therefore/because', preferred in writing over 그래서 (geuraeseo): 달라지므로 (dallajimeuro = since it varies).
-에 따라 means 'as/with' a change unfolds: 진행됨에 따라 (jinhaengdoem-e ttara = as it advances).
-던 바 (ba) is formal written shorthand for 'given the fact that': 높았던 바 (nopatdeon ba) = given that they were high. Bureaucratic prose favors this ending.
반면 contrasts two clauses ('whereas'): 줄여 주는 반면 (juryeo juneun banmyeon = while it reduces).
-(으)ㄴ 바에 따라 = 'as/per what is stated': 명시된 바에 따라 (myeongsidoen ba-e ttara = per what is stated).
-기 때문에 attaches to a stem to state cause: 크기 때문에 (keugi ttaemune = because it is wide).
-에 따라 = 'according to (a basis)': 결과에 따라 (gyeolgwa-e ttara = according to the results).
-기 때문에 marks a reason; on a past cause use -았/었기: 작용했기 때문에 (jag-yonghaetgi ttaemune = because it acted).
-(으)ㄹ수록 = 'the more ~, the more ~': 확대될수록 (hwakdaedoelsurok = the more it widens).
